# Olympic Games host cities — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/olympic-games.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/olympic-games.ttl`](../decks/olympic-games.ttl) · **Cards:** 55 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The host cities of all 55 Summer and Winter Olympic Games held from Athens 1896 to Milano Cortina 2026 (the Games cancelled in 1916, 1940 and 1944 and the 1906 Intercalated Games are not included). Front: the Games, e.g. "1912 Summer Olympics"; back: the host city in English and Swedish, both cities for the co-hosted 2026 Games, with a note where it helps (such as the 1956 equestrian events in Stockholm). Taken from Wikidata and checked against the IOC's list of Games (olympics.com) and Olympedia.

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of Games, the English and Swedish names of the Games and of the host cities, and the link from each Games to its host city all come from it, so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The IOC's olympics.com and Olympedia (both all rights reserved) and the English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the Wikidata data gave and supplied, as uncopyrightable facts restated in the compiler's own words, the reasons given in two notes (the 1956 quarantine rules for horses, from the IOC and the English Wikipedia; the 2020 postponement, which Wikidata also records); no wording, table or selection was copied from them. The selection is every held edition of two Wikidata series, which coincides with any complete list of Olympic Games because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list; the notes are the compiler's own wording of facts, and facts are not copyrightable. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' licences (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0, by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision; the IOC's text all rights reserved) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction. The deck was then cross-checked by independent AI reviewers (quality-control rounds 1–5: factual accuracy; language and translation; licensing, attribution and documentation; a final re-check of all cards and the documentation; a final full-deck review of facts and language), whose findings were verified and applied, and by machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Finding the Games in Wikidata: a first query (query 1) asked for items that are instances (P31) of Summer Olympic Games (Q159821) or Winter Olympic Games (Q82414) and returned nothing, because the editions are instances of edition classes (for example Q135976384 "Summer Olympic Games edition", as the entity API showed for the 1912 Games, Q8118, query 2). Query 3 instead selected every item whose P3450 (sports season of league or competition) is Q159821 or Q82414, with its start and end times (P580/P582), the truthy P276 (location) and P17 (country) values and the English and Swedish labels. The raw CSV was saved.
3. Selection: of the items from query 3, those with a start time (the Games actually held) from 1896 to 2026 became the cards: 30 Summer Games (1896–2024) and 25 Winter Games (1924–2026), 55 in all. The items for 1916, 1940 and 1944 (Summer) and 1940 and 1944 (Winter) have no start time: they were cancelled and are left out. Future Games (2028 onward) are left out. The 1906 Intercalated Games are not an edition of either series in Wikidata and are not counted by the IOC; they are left out (see the selection).
4. Host cities: the Games' P276 is not uniform. For 40 Games its truthy value includes the host city (sometimes with preferred rank and the qualifier "most precise value"). For 14 others the truthy values are venues only (for 1972 Summer the preferred value is the Olympic Stadium, which hides the normal-rank Munich). Query 4 listed every P276 statement of all ranks that is a human settlement, and query 5 every P276 statement (all ranks) of the Games without a city, with the venue's P131 (located in the administrative unit). For these 14 Games the city comes from the venue: e.g. 1952 Winter, Bislett Stadion (Q866409) located in Oslo Municipality (Q5245991), whose capital (P36) is Oslo (Q585); 1972 Winter, Makomanai Open Stadium (Q673240) in Minami-ku (Q1134027), itself in Sapporo (query 7). Each of these was also confirmed by an English alias of the Games item of the form "Oslo 1952" where Wikidata has one (queries 8 and 9). For 1960 Winter the preferred P276 is the ski resort Palisades Tahoe (Q2182804), whose English alias is "Squaw Valley"; the card gives the historical name Squaw Valley, used by the IOC and Olympedia.
5. English and Swedish names: the fronts are the Wikidata English and Swedish labels of the Games items, which follow one pattern ("1912 Summer Olympics" / "Olympiska sommarspelen 1912"). Query 6 fetched every English and Swedish label and alias of the host-city items. The English back is the city's English label or an alias that is the common short name (Chamonix rather than the commune name Chamonix-Mont-Blanc; Squaw Valley; Pyeongchang rather than Pyeongchang County; Lillehammer from the town item Q3745117, since the municipality item's Swedish label is "Lillehammers kommun"). The Swedish back is the Swedish label (Aten, Antwerpen, Helsingfors, Rom, München, Montréal, Moskva, Peking, Sankt Moritz, Saint Louis, Sotji, Turin, Milano …); for Oslo, which has no Swedish label, the multilingual (mul) label "Oslo". For the co-hosted 2026 Games the back names both cities, "Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo" / "Milano och Cortina d'Ampezzo".
6. Swedish check: the script fetch_games.py (query 9) fetched the Games items' labels, aliases and sitelinks and the introductions of their Swedish and English Wikipedia articles through the MediaWiki API. Every card's Swedish city name was found in the first sentence of the Swedish article that names the host city ("… hölls i Helsingfors i Finland …"); that sentence is quoted in the card's evidence. In quality-control round 3 every quoted Wikipedia introduction was fetched again with its revision id (query 21): the 62 quotes checked by revids.py were still verbatim, the two others (the Pyeongchang introduction, query 20, and the 1956 quarantine sentence) were checked against their own revisions, and each locator now links its revision. In round 4 all 64 quotes were checked again against the linked revisions (query 24) and all were verbatim; the Chamonix quote added in round 4 comes from query 23.
7. Cross-check against the IOC: the list of Games on olympics.com could not be fetched from the research environment (connections timed out, query 10), so the Internet Archive's capture of 2026-09-23 was downloaded (query 11) and the edition names in its page data were extracted; every card's city matched the IOC's name for the edition ("Stockholm 1912", "Turin 2006", "PyeongChang 2018", "Milano Cortina 2026" …). The IOC's Melbourne 1956 page (capture of 2026-01-13, query 12) was read for the equestrian events in Stockholm.
8. Cross-check against Olympedia: the Games overview (query 13) gives each edition's city, dates and status. All 55 cities agree with the cards (Olympedia writes local forms such as Athina, Roma, München, Torino and "Milano-Cortina d'Ampezzo"). It lists the 1956 equestrian Games in Stockholm in a separate row (10–17 June), the 1916, 1940 and 1944 Games as "Not held due to war", and the 1906 Games in a separate "Intercalated Games" table.
9. Notes: a back note was written, in the compiler's own words, only where it helps to answer or to avoid a wrong answer: the 1956 equestrian events in Stockholm, Tokyo 2020 held in 2021, the commune name Chamonix-Mont-Blanc, the present names of Squaw Valley, Sarajevo then in Yugoslavia, the Italian name Torino, Pyeongchang County and the IOC's spelling, and the official name and other sites of Milano Cortina 2026. Each note's facts were checked against Wikidata and the English (for Pyeongchang also the Swedish) Wikipedia introduction (for 1924 the introduction of the article on Chamonix, and Wikidata's official name, P1448, of Q83236), and the 1956 note also against the IOC and Olympedia. Two notes give a reason that is not in a Wikidata label or main value: the 1956 quarantine rules for horses (IOC Melbourne 1956 page and the English Wikipedia; Wikidata gives only the June 1956 equestrian qualifiers on the Stockholm location) and the 2020 postponement (also recorded in Wikidata's P580 qualifiers).
10. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata the English and Swedish labels of the Games (the front), the P276 link from the Games to the city or venue, the P131 chain from the venue to the city where needed, an English alias of the Games naming the city where one exists, and the English and Swedish labels or aliases of the city (the back); for Turin also the Italian label "Torino" given in the note. The builder accepts a multilingual (mul) label for any language, so a check on a language the item lacks (Oslo, Q585, has no sv label) passes on the mul label; the evidence says where that happens. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

All Olympic Games actually held, Summer and Winter, from the first modern Games (Athens 1896) to the most recent (Milano Cortina, February 2026): 30 Summer and 25 Winter Games. Left out: the Games cancelled because of the world wars (Summer 1916, 1940, 1944; Winter 1940, 1944), which were awarded but never held; the 1906 Intercalated Games in Athens, which the IOC does not count as Olympic Games (it is not in the IOC's list of editions, and Olympedia lists it apart from the Olympic Games); future Games (Los Angeles 2028 onward); the Youth Olympic Games, the Paralympic Games and the 1956 equestrian Games as a card of their own (they are part of the 1956 Summer Olympics and appear in that card's note). The back gives the host city, not the country or the venues; where events were spread over several places, the back names the host city the IOC names the Games after.

## Queries

**1. First attempt: Games as instances (P31) of Q159821/Q82414 (returned no rows)** (Wikidata: the editions of the Summer Olympic Games (Q159821) and Winter Olympic Games (Q82414), their locations (P276) and the labels of the Games and the host cities)

```
SELECT ?games ?type ?gamesEn ?gamesSv ?start ?end ?loc ?locEn ?locSv ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv WHERE {
  VALUES ?type { wd:Q159821 wd:Q82414 }
  ?games wdt:P31 ?type .
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P276 ?loc .
    OPTIONAL { ?loc rdfs:label ?locEn FILTER(LANG(?locEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?loc rdfs:label ?locSv FILTER(LANG(?locSv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P17 ?country .
    OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?games rdfs:label ?gamesEn FILTER(LANG(?gamesEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?games rdfs:label ?gamesSv FILTER(LANG(?gamesSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start ?games
```

**2. The 1912 Games' item, to see how editions are modelled (P31 edition class, P276 with ranks)** (Wikidata: the editions of the Summer Olympic Games (Q159821) and Winter Olympic Games (Q82414), their locations (P276) and the labels of the Games and the host cities)

```
curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&ids=Q8118&props=claims&format=json"
```

**3. Every edition of the two series (P3450) with start/end, truthy P276, P17 and labels (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q2.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) [the query text below was saved as q2.rq: the file names are one lower than the query numbers]** (Wikidata: the editions of the Summer Olympic Games (Q159821) and Winter Olympic Games (Q82414), their locations (P276) and the labels of the Games and the host cities)

```
SELECT ?games ?series ?class ?gamesEn ?gamesSv ?start ?end ?loc ?locEn ?locSv ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv WHERE {
  VALUES ?series { wd:Q159821 wd:Q82414 }
  ?games wdt:P3450 ?series .
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P31 ?class }
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P582 ?end }

  OPTIONAL { ?games wdt:P17 ?country .
    OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?games rdfs:label ?gamesEn FILTER(LANG(?gamesEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?games rdfs:label ?gamesSv FILTER(LANG(?gamesSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start ?games
```

**4. P276 statements of all ranks that are human settlements (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q3.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) [the query text below was saved as q3.rq: the file names are one lower than the query numbers]** (Wikidata: the editions of the Summer Olympic Games (Q159821) and Winter Olympic Games (Q82414), their locations (P276) and the labels of the Games and the host cities)

```
SELECT ?games ?gamesEn ?loc ?locEn ?rank ?locClass ?locClassEn WHERE {
  VALUES ?series { wd:Q159821 wd:Q82414 }

```
SELECT ?item ?kind ?lang ?text ?desc WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { wd:Q1524 wd:Q90 wd:Q38022 wd:Q84 wd:Q1754 wd:Q12892 wd:Q83236 wd:Q727 wd:Q68986 wd:Q192700 wd:Q65 wd:Q127043 wd:Q64 wd:Q585 wd:Q1757 wd:Q41158 wd:Q3141 wd:Q822230 wd:Q2182804 wd:Q220 wd:Q1735 wd:Q1490 wd:Q1289 wd:Q1489 wd:Q37951 wd:Q1726 wd:Q340 wd:Q649 wd:Q11194 wd:Q36312 wd:Q8684 wd:Q159469 wd:Q1492 wd:Q101341 wd:Q23556 wd:Q128849 wd:Q3130 wd:Q23337 wd:Q495 wd:Q956 wd:Q24639 wd:Q39420 wd:Q8678 wd:Q188624 wd:Q490 wd:Q5245991 }

## Quality control

6 rounds, 30 findings: 28 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 2 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (356 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's host city against Wikidata, the IOC's list of editions and Olympedia; the Swedish names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; the notes against Wikidata and the English Wikipedia. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 55 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata, the IOC and Olympedia agree on the host city of all 55 Games; no card follows a value that a better source contradicts, and no Wikidata check was skipped. The discrepancies are in how Wikidata models the location (14 Games have only venues as truthy P276 values, 1960's preferred P276 is the ski resort under its present name, 1956 has Stockholm as a second, normal-rank location), handled by checking the venue's P131 chain and an alias of the Games. Builder checks cover the front labels, the Games-to-city link and the back labels of every card.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| summer-1956 | Wikidata P276 has Melbourne (preferred) and Stockholm (normal rank); the equestrian events were held in Stockholm in June 1956. Naming both cities on the back would make the Games look co-hosted, which the IOC and Olympedia do not do. | Back Melbourne (the IOC's Melbourne 1956); the note says the equestrian events were held in Stockholm in June 1956 because of Australia's quarantine rules for horses (IOC Melbourne 1956 page; Olympedia's separate Equestrian row, 10–17 June). The builder checks only the truthy (preferred) Melbourne value. | fixed |
| winter-1960 | Wikidata's preferred P276 is Palisades Tahoe (Q2182804), the ski resort's present name; a normal-rank P276 is Olympic Valley (Q822230), the community's present name; a deprecated P276 is Yokuts Valley (Q2141628), a different place in Fresno County formerly also called Squaw Valley. The IOC and Olympedia call the Games Squaw Valley 1960. | Back "Squaw Valley" (the name of the place in 1960, an alias of both Wikidata items, and the IOC's and Olympedia's name); the note gives the present names. Checks: P276 Q2182804, its alias "Squaw Valley", Q822230's English and Swedish alias "Squaw Valley" and the Games' alias "Squaw Valley 1960". | fixed |
| winter-1924 | Wikidata's English and Swedish labels of the host commune are "Chamonix-Mont-Blanc"; the IOC ("Chamonix 1924") and Olympedia ("Chamonix") use the short name. | Back "Chamonix" (an English and Swedish alias in Wikidata); the note gives the commune's official name. | fixed |
| winter-1952 | Wikidata's P276 for the 1952 Winter Games is only Bislett Stadion, located in Oslo Municipality (Q5245991), not the city item Oslo (Q585), which has no Swedish label (only the multilingual label "Oslo"). | Back Oslo; checks P276 Bislett Stadion, its P131 Oslo Municipality, the Games' alias "Oslo 1952" and Q585's labels (the builder accepts the mul label for Swedish). Same approach (venue P131 plus Games alias) for 1964 Winter, 1972 Summer and Winter, 1984 Summer and Winter, 1988 Summer, 1992, 1994, 1998, 2002, 2006, 2010 and 2018 Winter. | fixed |
| winter-1994 | The venue chain ends at Lillehammer Municipality (Q101341), whose Swedish label is "Lillehammers kommun". | Back Lillehammer, with the label checks on the town item Q3745117 (English and Swedish label "Lillehammer"). | fixed |
| winter-2018 | The venue chain ends at Pyeongchang County (Q188624, English label "Pyeongchang County"); the IOC writes "PyeongChang 2018". | Back "Pyeongchang" (English alias and Swedish label of Q188624, the Swedish Wikipedia's form); the note says it is Pyeongchang County and gives the IOC's spelling. | fixed |

Check P580 year 2021. | fixed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 55 cards: every host city against Olympedia's editions tables, the English Wikipedia list of host cities and a SPARQL query of the edition items; notes; Wikidata checks spot-checked through the API.

No wrong facts. One documentation error (round 0 claimed a check on Q2182804's alias "Squaw Valley" that did not exist) and two suggestions on the 2018 Swedish note and the Swedish Oslo check. All three verified against the Wikidata API (query 17) and applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| winter-1960 | Round 0 says the checks include the alias "Squaw Valley" of Q2182804 (the preferred P276), but there was no such check, so the back text was never tied to the item the P276 check verifies. | Verified: Q2182804 has en aliases "Squaw Valley Ski Resort", "Squaw Valley Alpine Meadows" and "Squaw Valley". Added the check Q2182804 en = "Squaw Valley", which makes the round 0 log true, and listed the aliases in the evidence. | fixed |
| winter-2018 | The Swedish note left out that Pyeongchang is a county, the disambiguation the English note gives. | Verified against the Swedish Wikipedia article "Pyeongchang" ("en landskommun (gun) i provinsen Gangwon i Sydkorea") and Q188624's sv alias "Pyeongchang-gun". The reviewer's "härad" is not the Swedish Wikipedia's term, so the note uses "landskommun (gun)": sv "Landskommunen (gun) Pyeongchang i provinsen Gangwon i Sydkorea; IOK skriver PyeongChang 2018."; en made parallel, "Pyeongchang County in Gangwon Province, South Korea; …". The Swedish article was added to the evidence. | fixed |
| winter-1952 | The Swedish "Oslo" checks pass only through Q585's multilingual label, and the P131 chain ends at Oslo Municipality (Q5245991), not at Q585, whose labels are checked. | Verified: Q585 has only en and mul labels; Q5245991 has P36 (capital) Q585 and Q585 has P1376 (capital of) Q5245991. Added the check Q5245991 P36 = Q585, which links the chain to the labelled item, and the evidence now says that the Swedish "Oslo" is the mul label. | fixed |

No other Swedish text names the 1906 Games. | fixed |
| deck | The last sentence of the Swedish description has no subject ("Hämtad från …"), and "de delade spelen 2026" can read as "the divided Games". | Reworded: "… båda städerna för spelen 2026, som hade två värdstäder, … Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata och kontrollerade mot …". | fixed |
| deck | The Swedish description uses straight English quotation marks. | description.sv now uses the Swedish ”Olympiska sommarspelen 1912”. | fixed |
| summer-2020 | The Swedish note ("Uppskjutna …: hölls …, fortfarande som Tokyo 2020") is a literal translation without a subject to agree with. | sv: "Sköts upp ett år på grund av covid-19-pandemin och hölls i juli–augusti 2021, men fortfarande under namnet Tokyo 2020."; en made parallel: "Postponed by a year because of the COVID-19 pandemic and held in July–August 2021, still under the name Tokyo 2020." | fixed |
